title: 👋 Hi, I’m Eugeni!
text:
👋 Hi, I’m Eugeni!

I’m a mobility researcher with a background in environmental management, transport planning, data analytics, and law. I’m passionate about cycling, data visualisation, and maps, which shape my research on how people move and how the built environment influences travel choices.
I hold a PhD in Data Analytics and Society from the University of Leeds, where I researched cycling and socioeconomic disadvantage. I later worked there as a postdoctoral researcher in active travel and data science at the Institute for Transport Studies.
Now, I’m based at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, working with GEMOTT (the Research Group on Mobility, Transport and Territory), mainly on the ATRAPA project, which explores public acceptability of sustainable active-travel urban interventions. I’m also involved in research on active commuting to school and big data mobility projects.
This website brings together my research, publications, interactive resources, and field observations. I hope you find something of interest. If you’d like to get in touch, you can reach me at eugenividal [at] hotmail [dot] com.

title: Research
text:
My research focuses on active travel, cycling, spatial data, and inequalities in mobility. I am particularly interested in how the built environment shapes travel behaviour and how data can help us better understand transport systems.





The Active Travel Backlash Paradox
Research on the public acceptability of sustainable active-travel interventions and their social, political, and spatial implications.

Validating OpenStreetMap for detecting cycling-infrastructure change (Barcelona, 2015–2023) (paper in preparation, WP1)




Research on social inequalities, neighbourhood context, and active commuting to and from school.



Contribution to an R package for accessing and analysing large Spanish mobility datasets.






Supporting Active Travel Using Road-lighting at Night.



Cycle Route Uptake & Scenario Estimation tool for Transport Infrastructure Ireland.




My PhD thesis, Cycling and Socioeconomic Disadvantage, examined inequalities in cycling participation, infrastructure access, travel behaviour, and safety.

I am a mobility researcher with a background in transport planning, environmental management, data analytics and law. My work focuses on active travel, cycling, spatial data, urban interventions and social inequalities in mobility.

Barcelona, Spain · December 2024–present

Working on the ATRAPA (The Active Travel Backlash Paradox) project.
Developing spatial analysis of urban interventions and public response.
Supporting the development of datasets linking active-travel interventions with electoral outcomes.
